title: Console UX notes — Dedicated staged rollouts: stage timeline, promotion confirmations, hold semantics, gate evidence
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture UX decisions + open questions for Dedicated staged rollouts in Console: stage timeline component, promotion confirmation flows, “Hold” semantics, and how gate evidence is presented to customer admins vs Redwood operators.
- Audience: Console eng + Design + PM + SRE reviewers.
- Non-goal: full visual spec (this is notes / copy / interaction details; final pixels in Figma / DES-431).

Context / user types
- Customer admin / operator (Dedicated customer): wants safe upgrades, clear “can I promote?” and “why blocked?”, minimal noise, needs auditability.
- Redwood SRE / oncall: wants fast diagnosis, clarity on gate source failures, and safe escape hatches (hold/abort/force) with audit.
- PM expectation: the MVP needs to be usable for design partners without hand-holding, but we can keep gate configurability limited.

1) Stage timeline component — behavior + states
Goal: make the rollout feel deterministic and auditable. Users should always be able to answer:
- What stage are we in?
- What changed at each stage?
- Are gates passing? If not, which signal(s), and what can I do?
- What actions are available right now (Promote / Abort / Hold)?

1.1 Timeline layout (high level)
- Horizontal stage “chips” with percent (or partition size) + name. Default set currently: 1% → 10% → 50% → 100% (per product thread). Some customers want 0% as “prep” but that’s effectively Draft/Planned.
- Each stage chip shows:
  - Stage label: “Canary (1%)”, “Ramp (10%)”, etc. (editable names but keep percent prominent)
  - Status icon: Pending / Running / Passed / Failed / Held / Aborted / Completed
  - Mini health summary: e.g., “3/3 gates passing” or “1 gate failing”
- Selecting a stage opens a right-side panel (or lower panel) with:
  - What is routed to this stage (model version/runtime build/policy hash)
  - Gate details (see section 4)
  - Stage time window: start time, min duration requirement (if any), sample size notes
  - Per-region breakdown (collapsed by default; expand for multi-region Dedicated pools)

1.2 Stage statuses (UI copy + semantics)
- Planned: not started. Copy: “Not started”
- Running: traffic is being routed to stage partition. Copy: “Receiving traffic”
- Passing: currently meeting all gate criteria but may still be within min-duration. Copy: “Gates passing” + “Minimum duration: X remaining” if applicable
- Eligible to promote: passing + duration/sample requirements satisfied. Copy: “Ready to promote”
- Failed: one or more gates failing OR gate evaluation is fail-closed due to missing/stale data. Copy: “Promotion blocked”
- Held: explicitly frozen by an operator/admin. Copy: “Held (no automatic changes)”
- Aborted: rollout aborted; traffic should be routed back to previous stable target. Copy: “Aborted”
- Completed: 100% stage stable. Copy: “Completed”

Important nuance: “Unknown” vs “Failing”
- Proposed: treat telemetry staleness as a first-class state: “Insufficient data” (not “failing” visually).
- However, promotion should be blocked when gates are unknown (fail-closed) unless override permissions are present.
- UI should show:
  - Yellow/gray “Insufficient data” pill per gate
  - Banner: “Promotion blocked: waiting for sufficient telemetry (last datapoint: 6m ago).”

1.3 Promotions + timeline annotations
- Timeline should annotate action events as markers:
  - “Promoted to 10%”
  - “Held by <actor> (reason)”
  - “Aborted by <actor> (reason)”
  - “Force-promoted by <actor> (reason)” (admin only; visible to customer if they have the permission + audit visibility rules)
- Each marker links to an Audit event detail view (even MVP should at least deep-link to the audit log table filtered by rollout_id).

2) Promotion confirmation UX
Goal: reduce accidental promotions, especially when a canary partition changes effective capacity (risk: 429s / queue depth spikes). Confirmation should force an explicit acknowledgment of what’s about to change + current gate status.

2.1 Promote button placement and enablement
- Primary CTA: “Promote” displayed when:
  - Rollout state = Running
  - Current stage gates = all pass AND min-duration/sample satisfied
- If gates failing/unknown:
  - Replace CTA with disabled “Promote” + “Blocked” tooltip
  - Provide secondary “Hold” (always) and “Abort” (always) actions
- If user has override permissions (admin): show “Force promote” as overflow action (kebab) not as a primary CTA.

2.2 Promote confirmation modal (standard)
Modal title: “Promote rollout to Stage N: <stage name> (<X%>)?”
Content (structured, not a wall of text):
- Summary section (top):
  - Current stage: “10% (Ramp)” → Next stage: “50% (Ramp)” (show exact percent)
  - Change payload (diff):
    - Model: llama-3.1-70b-instruct v2025-02-01 → v2025-02-20
    - Runtime: rw-serving 1.18.2 → 1.19.0
    - Routing policy: policy hash abc → def
  - “This will shift approximately <estimated requests/sec> to the new target.” (Est is optional; if we can’t estimate, omit; don’t lie.)

- Gate snapshot:
  - “All required gates are passing”
  - Show 3–5 high-level gates inline (Latency p95, Error rate, Saturation/headroom, OOM rate, Drops/429s) with current observed value vs threshold.
  - Link: “View full gate evidence” (opens the stage detail panel without losing modal context OR opens a new tab).

- Required acknowledgement checkbox (for customer admins too):
  - Checkbox: “I understand this will increase traffic to the new version and may impact latency/errors if issues emerge.”
  - If we want less friction for frequent promotions, make this checkbox only for stage jumps >= 50% or only for admin actions. (Open question.)

Buttons:
- Primary: “Promote to <X%>”
- Secondary: “Cancel”
- Optional tertiary: “Promote and hold” (NOT recommended for MVP; can be confusing)

2.3 Promote confirmation modal (force promote)
Force promote is for admin/Redwood operators only.
Modal title: “Force promote (bypass gates)?”
- Warning banner (red): “This bypasses required gates and will be recorded in audit logs.”
- Required fields:
  - Reason (textarea; required)
  - Ticket link (optional but encouraged; auto-suggest Jira/Linear format)
- Gate snapshot still shown, but with explicit “Not satisfied” labels.
- Copy should mention: “Force promote may violate SLOs. Consider Hold or Abort instead.”

3) “Hold” semantics — definition, UI, and edge cases
Goal: a safe “pause” that stops automatic progression and optionally stabilizes routing decisions while investigation happens.

3.1 What Hold means (proposed)
- Hold is a rollout-level state: traffic remains at the current stage partition and no automatic promotion occurs.
- Gate evaluation continues (we still compute gates for visibility), but we do not auto-abort or auto-promote while held.
- Hold does NOT roll back. It freezes.

3.2 When Hold is used
- Investigating flaky metrics / telemetry lag
- Waiting for business approval window
- Partial region impairment where we want to pause progression
- Customer asks: “pause while we run manual QA against the canary”

3.3 Hold actions in UI
- Always show Hold as secondary action in header when rollout is Running.
- When held, show “Resume” primary action (instead of Promote).
- Hold requires a reason (short text) + optional link to incident/ticket.

3.4 Hold timeout and stale holds
Open question from platform thread: do we auto-timeout holds?
- Proposal: default no auto-timeout in v1 (avoid surprising resumption). Instead show “Held for 3d 4h” with a callout: “Consider aborting or resuming.”
- For Redwood internal SRE view, optionally add “Nudge” reminder.

3.5 Hold vs Abort vs Rollback (user mental model)
- Hold: pause at current stage
- Abort: revert to last stable target and mark rollout aborted
- Rollback: (might be same as abort semantics in v1). We should avoid a separate “Rollback” verb unless platform semantics differ.

Copy suggestion in header tooltip:
- Hold: “Pauses the rollout at the current stage. Traffic stays split as-is.”
- Abort: “Stops the rollout and routes all traffic back to the previous stable version.”

4) Presenting gate evidence to customers
Goal: customers want transparency but not an overwhelming SRE dashboard. Also we need to avoid exposing internal-only signal names when not appropriate.

4.1 Gate evidence design principles
- Lead with “what decision is blocked and why” (pass/fail + reason)
- Always show: observed value, threshold, evaluation window, and sample size (or a proxy)
- Show per-region only when it’s meaningful; otherwise default to aggregate with ability to expand
- Make missing data explicit, with timestamp and suspected reason (telemetry lag) rather than silent emptiness (SUP-28605 symptom).

4.2 Gate evidence panel structure
Gate Evidence section (within stage detail panel):
- Header: “Gates” with overall status summary: “4 passing • 1 failing • 0 insufficient data”
- Each gate row:
  - Gate name (customer-friendly):
    - “Request error rate” (not “5xx_rate”)
    - “Latency (p95)”
    - “GPU headroom”
    - “OOM rate”
    - “Request throttling (429)”
  - Status pill: Passing / Failing / Insufficient data
  - Observed vs threshold: “0.31% ≤ 0.50%”
  - Window: “Last 15m”
  - “View details” expand

Expanded details:
- Small chart thumbnail (optional; if not in MVP, show a sparkline-like ASCII or omit and rely on numbers)
- Breakdown:
  - By region (us-east-1, eu-west-1) if multi-region pool
  - By route (chat/completions vs embeddings) only if cardinality is safe and meaningful. Default: no.
- Query provenance (internal vs external):
  - Customer view: do not show raw PromQL/SQL. Show “Computed from stage-tagged metrics.”
  - Redwood internal view: show query ID / link to dashboard panel.

4.3 Handling missing / mismatched telemetry
We need explicit UI states because “empty panel” reads as broken:
- If stage tags not present / mismatch:
  - Banner: “No stage telemetry found yet for this stage. This may take up to 5 minutes after promotion.”
  - Show last event time + ingestion lag (if available)
  - Action: “Refresh” and link “Troubleshooting telemetry” (internal only)
- If telemetry stale:
  - Banner: “Telemetry is delayed (last datapoint 12m ago). Promotion is blocked until data is current.”

4.4 Customer messaging when gates fail
We should provide a consistent “next step” suggestion (but avoid telling them exactly how to run SRE).
- Gate failure banner copy (customer view):
  - “Promotion blocked: Latency (p95) exceeded threshold for 10 minutes.”
  - Secondary line: “Review the failing gate(s). Consider holding the rollout while you investigate, or abort to return to the previous stable version.”
- Provide a “Hold rollout” CTA in the failure banner.

4.5 Which evidence is shown to customers vs internal
Proposal:
- Customer admins see:
  - Gate name, status, observed vs threshold, window
  - Per-region summary if relevant
  - A link to their own logs/metrics is out of scope; we only show Redwood-derived evidence.
- Redwood internal operators see additionally:
  - Underlying metric IDs, query IDs, related dashboards
  - Node/GPU health specifics if it risks exposing infra topology (careful)
  - “Debug” metadata: stage_id labels, sample counts, ingestion lag, errors

5) Audit trail visibility in Console
- Every Promote/Abort/Hold/Resume/Force-promote action should be visible as:
  - Timeline marker (quick context)
  - Audit log table entry (authoritative record)
- For customer view: show actor as “<user email>” or “Redwood operator” depending on RBAC + whether the actor is internal.
- Include “reason” when provided.

6) UX guardrails for Dedicated pool partitioning (capacity constraints)
We’ve already seen canary partitions cause effective capacity drop (SUP-28522). We should add a UX hint when the stage is very small relative to reservation.

Ideas (not all MVP):
- Pre-flight warning before starting/promoting if stage partition would allocate < N replicas or < min headroom.
- In Promote confirmation modal: show “Capacity check” row:
  - “Estimated replicas in next stage: 2 (minimum recommended: 4)” → warn + link to guidelines.
- If platform blocks creation/promotion due to validation, surface error copy that’s actionable:
  - “Cannot promote: next stage would allocate fewer than 2 replicas in eu-west-1. Adjust stages or reservation size.”

7) Open questions (needs alignment)
1) Do we require min-duration at each stage in v1?
   - SRE leaning yes (5m or 15m) + minimum sample size. UX impact: stage looks “passing” but not “ready”.
2) How prominent is “Force promote”?
   - Strong preference: hide in overflow; require admin permission + reason.
3) Do we show “quality regression” gates in customer UI?
   - If we do, need careful copy; customers may interpret as Redwood judging their prompts.
   - Maybe only show when configured and with customer-provided eval set.
4) Streaming sessions behavior on promote/abort:
   - If in-flight pinned to old stage, we should say so somewhere (“Existing streams continue on current target”).
5) Naming: “Abort” vs “Rollback”
   - Suggest “Abort rollout” with subtext “Routes traffic back to previous stable.”
6) Customer-visible vs Redwood-only gate list
   - Some gates are operational (GPU ECC errors) that may be too infra-specific. Option: show a simplified “GPU health” rollup.

8) Proposed copy snippets (WIP)
- Gate status summary:
  - “Ready to promote”
  - “Promotion blocked”
  - “Insufficient data”
- Hold tooltip:
  - “Pause the rollout at the current stage. Traffic stays split as-is.”
- Missing telemetry banner:
  - “We haven’t received stage telemetry for this stage yet. This can take a few minutes after a promotion.”
- Force promote warning:
  - “This action bypasses safety gates and may impact availability. A reason is required and will be recorded.”

9) Next steps / TODO
- Kenji: sync with Marissa on whether min-duration is required for MVP (affects timeline states + copy).
- Console backend: confirm evidence response includes (observed_value, threshold, window, status_reason, data_freshness) per gate (see Slack contract thread).
- Observability: confirm naming conventions for customer-friendly gate labels.
- Design (DES-431): incorporate these states into timeline component + modal.
- Add to validation checklist: reproduce SUP-28605 (gate evidence empty) and ensure UI shows explicit “no data” state, not blank.
